key_insight: Aggregate scores can mask next-visit diagnosis prediction weaknesses; LONGINUS combines retrieval and memory to improve transition-specific performance among LLM-based methods.
clinical_relevance: Distinguishing persistent, newly recorded, and recurrent diagnoses may make evaluation more informative for clinical prediction research, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Evaluate diagnosis-set size, long-tailed labels, temporal transitions, and observed history depth.
Combine retrieved patient-record evidence with structured memory of the patient trajectory.
Preserve predictions shared across views and adjudicate disagreements without revealing their source.
evidence_signal: Across MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV with four LLM backbones, LONGINUS led LLM-based methods on transition-specific performance in nearly all settings, while repeating the last visit outperformed most LLM approaches overall.
watch_item: Cross-view agreement is a reliability heuristic, not proof of correctness, and the abstract does not establish prospective clinical benefit.
paper_title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication
